names: Dextrin (Dextrins, roasted starch white and yellow) (stabiliser)

more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Dextrins are starch carbohydrates whose chains have been partly broken down. FDA describes manufacture by dry heating several edible starches, sometimes after treatment with suitable acids or alkalis. Food functions include formulation assistance, thickening, stabilisation and surface finishing. Different dextrin preparations can differ in colour and in the extent of starch breakdown.
more_info.origin: Produced by dry heating edible starch from sources such as corn, potato, wheat, rice, tapioca or sago. The starch may first be treated with suitable acids, alkalis or pH-control agents and then dried. This process partly breaks down a plant-derived starch carbohydrate.
